elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Renewal remains automatic ("will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term ... unless either party notifies"), and the conditional preferred elements below (12-month cap, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder, CPI/3% cap) are not all satisfied, so the mutual-written-agreement default is not displaced.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Renewal term is "equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment" — untouched by the redline; if an Order Form/Service Option Attachment term is multi-year, renewals are multi-year. Repair by expressly fixing each renewal term at twelve (12) months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause requires notice "at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term" — 60 days exceeds the preferred 30-day ceiling.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in the rendered language; IBM owes no pre-renewal notice. Repair by inserting an express IBM obligation to notify Customer at least 60 days before each automatic renewal.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Inserted cap is "one hundred five percent (105%) of the charges in effect for the immediately preceding term" — a 5% cap with no CPI comparator, short of the lesser-of-CPI-and-3% preferred standard.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Operative text now reads "unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term" (down from ninety (90) days). The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a mechanical miss: the numeral "sixty (60)" is present in the rendered clause and the window is exactly 60 days.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Charges for each renewal term will not exceed one hundred five percent (105%) of the charges in effect for the immediately preceding term of the applicable Service Option Attachment" — a per-renewal uplift ceiling of 5%.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the non-renewal notice window is cut from 90 to 60 days (satisfying the ≤60-day ceiling) and renewal charges are capped at 105% of the prior term (satisfying the ≤5% ceiling).

Disregard the failing regex 'non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days — number not found'; on inspection the rendered clause states 'at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term', so the element is substantively met and the check is a formatting/parse artefact.

Preferred level fails on four counts: renewal term is still 'equal in duration to the previous term' rather than 12 months; opt-out notice is 60 rather than 30 days; there is no IBM 60-day pre-renewal reminder; and the uplift cap is 5% rather than the lesser of CPI and 3%.

Minimality holds: exactly two edits, both tied to fallback elements (numeral change 90→60 and one concise cap sentence). No survival tails, expense language, procedures, or unrelated deletions were introduced, and the retained Section 13.1 change/termination mechanics were left intact.

Intent is preserved: the mutual either-party non-renewal structure, the Section 13.1 mid-term price-change right, the 90-day notice, the non-retroactivity sentence and Customer's 30-day no-charge termination election all survive without dangling references.

Caution (not an element failure): retained Section 13.1 lets IBM change Service Option Attachment prices after 12 months on 90 days' notice with no percentage limit. The new sentence is a specific ceiling on renewal-term charges and should control at renewal, but if the counterparty resists that reading, the cleanest repair is to open the inserted sentence with 'Notwithstanding Section 13.1,' rather than adding further operative text.

Caution (outside the fallback checklist): because renewal duration still tracks the prior term, a multi-year Order Form term produces automatic multi-year renewals, which is walk-away territory under this rule. If any Service Option Attachment term exceeds 12 months, escalate and fix the renewal term to twelve (12) months rather than settling at the fallback.
